heroHeadline: UNAMA: 372 Afghan Civilians Killed in First 3 Months of 2026 Conflict — Highest Quarterly Toll Since 2011; Taliban Besieges TOLO News Offices
heroSubtitle: On May 13, 2026 (Day 77 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan published its first quarterly civilian casualty report for the 2026 conflict, documenting 372 Afghan civilians killed and 397 injured between January 1 and March 31 — the highest such toll UNAMA has recorded since 2011. The report attributed 64% of civilian deaths to Pakistani airstrikes and 34% to cross-border artillery. The single deadliest incident was the March 16 strike on the Omid Drug Rehabilitation Center in Kabul (269 UNAMA-confirmed dead). The UNAMA report provides the first authoritative third-party record of the conflict's human cost and adds significant international accountability pressure on Pakistan. Separately, the Taliban confirmed the detention of two TOLO News journalists — presenter Mansoor Niazi (arrested May 7) and political editor Imran Danish (arrested May 9) — while besieging TOLO's Kabul offices. The Committee to Protect Journalists called for their immediate release. The formal diplomatic impasse from May 12 — the IEA's categorical rejection of Pakistan's Bannu attack evidence as 'baseless and unfounded' — stands unresolved. Pakistan COAS Munir's 'logical conclusion' warning (May 11) remains operative. No Urumqi Round 2 date has been set. No formal ceasefire exists.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
